The chairs scrape as the crowd breaks up. I fold my notes and set the glass of water down on the lectern.
I am uneasy, and the lectern edge is warmer under my hand than my hand is. The words I still have to say sit in my throat like a swallowed stone.

steps.title: Bring them together

He knew Kitty before I did, and he fought in Spain while I talked about it from a platform. I wanted him to hear it from me plainly.
The lectern is still at my elbow and my notes lie on it, gone soft at the corners from my hands.
I am relieved and a little light in the chest, and the rows of faces in the hall have stopped weighing on me.
